title: How PeerDAS came to Ethereum
intro: Rollups need room to post their data, and Ethereum's answer was blobs. This is how it went from every node downloading every blob (EIP-4844, the Dencun upgrade) to nodes holding and sampling only a slice, PeerDAS (EIP-7594), which went live with the Fusaka upgrade. Along the way, the argument was how fast to raise blob counts, at what cost to home stakers, and with what priority. It is told in talks, research posts and forum replies.

stops.title: EIP-4844 starts small: two blobs a block
stops.body: Four days after that call, EIP-4844 was changed to cut its starting capacity from a target of about 1 MB and a limit of about 2 MB per block to about 0.25 MB and 0.5 MB, a target of two blobs and a maximum of four. The EIP says these small initial limits are intended to minimize the strain on the network.
stops.note: Primary source: EIPs pull request 5863 'Reduce Throughput' (commit 89b85203, 14 Nov 2022): MAX_DATA_GAS_PER_BLOCK 2**21 to 2**19 and TARGET_DATA_GAS_PER_BLOCK 2**20 to 2**18; new 'Throughput' section: 'a target of 2 blobs (0.25 MB) and maximum of 4 blobs (0.5 MB) per block. These small initial limits are intended to minimize the strain on the network'. Micah Zoltu names the PR on ACDE #149 (segment 91: 'this PR to change its throughput ... helps a little bit but it is still strictly an increase'). The call in which it was agreed was not identified: the EIP-4844 implementers calls of 8 and 15 Nov 2022 were not searched for it beyond a keyword scan.

stops.author: Danny Ryan
stops.source_title: PeerDAS -- a simpler DAS approach using battle-tested p2p components
stops.note: The founding post of PeerDAS: reuse the networking Ethereum already runs instead of inventing a new one, and keep each honest node's work close to 4844's.

lines.text: The intent of a PeerDAS design is to reuse well known, battle-tested p2p components already in production in Ethereum to bring additional DA scale beyond that of 4844 while keeping the minimum amount of work of honest nodes in the same realm as 4844 (downloading < 1MB per slot).
Importantly, any DAS solution will rely upon nodes of various types and the assumptions we can make about them.

stops.author: Dankrad
stops.note: A sharp question, not a verdict: written about SubnetDAS, a sibling proposal to PeerDAS, not about PeerDAS itself. Dankrad says sampling is only safe if everyone converges on available even against a malicious majority, and that one disrupted row subnet could stop reconstruction under that construction. He says himself he is unsure how reliable such a subnet is and that it needs research.

lines.text: Once the DA threshold (e.g. 50% in this proposal) is reached, we want all nodes to agree that the data is available. This property should be robust even if a majority of validators is malicious, for obvious reasons.
Note that under the given construction, it suffices to disrupt a single row subnet to completely stop reconstruction -- all samples would be incomplete if that subnet is not able to do its part.

stops.author: Francesco (fradamt)
stops.source_title: From 4844 to Danksharding: a path to scaling Ethereum DA
stops.note: The staging plan that PeerDAS became: do not jump to full Danksharding, break the road into steps that raise throughput while barely raising bandwidth.

lines.text: Given its ambitious nature, we think it is best to further break down the road from 4844 to Danksharding into more manageable steps, reducing the complexity and risk of each upgrade and allowing us to gradually scale the data layer throughput.

A possible path goes through intermediate stages, where we gradually introduce all cryptographic and networking components, and gradually obtain more scalability and feature-completeness, while at most minimally increasing the bandwidth requirements compared to 4844.

stops.title: Blobs go live on mainnet in Dencun
stops.body: Dencun (Cancun-Deneb) activated on 13 March 2024. ethereum.org's upgrade history describes its EIP-4844, proto-danksharding, as introducing data blobs that let rollups post data to Mainnet for a short period of time.
stops.note: Primary source: ethereum.org/en/history (read 10 Nov 2026): Dencun (Cancun-Deneb), Mar 13, 2024, 1:55:35 PM UTC, block 19,426,587; EIP-4844 'Proto-Danksharding'. The page states no blob target or maximum, so the body does not. Also confirmed: EF blog Dencun mainnet announcement (epoch 269568, 13 March 2024 13:55 UTC; written before activation). Closes the gap noted on x-09 ('leaves no stop that says Dencun went live').

stops.title: PeerDAS is put into Fulu, the fork after Pectra
stops.body: On the 31 October 2024 consensus-layer call, the chair said he heard no opposition to moving the PeerDAS EIP (EIP-7594) into the Fulu fork, on top of Electra (Pectra), so that PeerDAS activates with Fulu. The call had named the pair of Fulu and Osaka Fusaka on 22 August 2024. One developer asked to keep it separately triggered until sure; that went to the next execution-layer call.
stops.note: Primary source: our transcript of ACDC #145 (Alex Stokes, segments 80 to 97: 'having PeerDAS be Fulu, have it activate at Fulu ... there's no opposition to moving ahead on the CL in this direction'; Barnabas Busa, segments 85 to 93, asks whether to keep it separately triggered as EIP-7594 until sure, because activating Fulu would also activate Osaka and EOF on the execution side; Stokes will take that to the next ACDE). The name Fusaka (Fulu plus Osaka) was picked on ACDC #140 (22 Aug 2024, segments 215 to 216). Fills the gap between s-06's 'descheduled from Pectra' and Fusaka.

stops.title: Pectra goes ahead with a higher blob target and limit
stops.body: On the 28 November 2024 consensus-layer call, after hearing from the ethPandaOps data and from developers on both sides, the chair said he was hearing a lot of support for EIP-7691's target of 6 and maximum of 9 blobs, up from 3 and 6, and later asked whether the call was happy moving ahead with 6/9 and the fee update, on the strength of support in the chat. The call's closing review of the Pectra devnet 5 changes listed EIP-7691 and asked its authors to update the fee update fraction.
stops.note: Primary source: our transcript of ACDC #146 (Alex Stokes: 'I am hearing a lot of support for 6/9 ... I'd like to go ahead and just make the decision now'; closing items: 'from this list here on this issue, 7691 ... would need an update for the update fraction', authors asked to handle it) and ethereum/pm call_146.md items 146.5 to 146.7. The update fraction was settled on ACDE #201 (5 Dec 2024, Ansgar Dietrichs) and the EIP text updated the same day (EIPs commit b45ee372). The call itself does not read out a vote; the body says only what was said.

stops.author: Mikel Cortes (cortze)
stops.source_title: Bandwidth Availability in Ethereum: Regional Differences and Network Impacts
stops.note: The second measurement behind the Pectra increase, from ProbeLab, measured 23 to 28 Nov 2024 and discussed on the 28 Nov call: it sees no critical objection to 6/9, but notes a loaded first four seconds of the slot, and asks for bandwidth-saving work because more blobs will be needed.

lines.text: 60% of nodes deployed in Europe or the US have bandwidth availability of more than 20Mbps, while only 20% of nodes deployed in Australia can go above 20Mbps. This is not related to line speed availability in Australia, but rather it is due to the fact that 65% of Ethereum nodes are located in Europe or the US and therefore geographically far from Asia-based nodes.
Given the above, our take is that we don’t see any critical objection to the current desired blob target and max values of 6/9 discussed in the All Core Dev CL Call on Thursday 28th of November.

At the same time, we expect that nodes will be stressed with regard to bandwidth availability during the 1st and 4th seconds of the slot, especially assuming the number of duplicate messages that Gossipsub inevitably propagates through the network.

lines.text: BPO forks are simple Ethereum forks that only change two parameters: blob targets and blob limits.

There are two generally agreed upon priorities with blobs: 1) ensure solo stakers with limited bandwidth can continue to produce blocks, and 2) provide DA scale to L2s to keep tx costs competitive. More flexibility to tweak blob parameters will help Ethereum thread the needle between the two.

stops.body: PeerDAS (EIP-7594) went live with the Fusaka upgrade on 3 December 2025. Two blob-parameter-only forks then raised the blob target and limit in steps, to 10 and 15 on 9 December and to 14 and 21 on 7 January 2026.
stops.note: Two primary sources, both on the Ethereum Foundation blog. That the upgrade went live with Data Availability Sampling, and that the target is now 14 blobs with a limit of 21, is from Checkpoint #8 (20 Jan 2026, linked). The dates and numbers are from the Fusaka mainnet announcement (blog.ethereum.org/2025/11/06/fusaka-mainnet-announcement, Protocol Coordination Team): activation at epoch 411392 on 3 December 2025 21:49:11 UTC; BPO1 on 9 December 2025 and BPO2 on 7 January 2026; targets and limits 6 and 9, then 10 and 15, then 14 and 21. That announcement was written before activation, so it is cited for the schedule only. Not in our catalogue; we link to the blog and never copy it.

lines.text: Increasing the blob count incurs a clear worsening of both block latency and attestation rate on almost all observed networks, both before and after PeerDAS alike.
Additionally, we observed a worse tail latency after PeerDAS compared to before, and the tail latency increasingly worsens as the blob count increases.
However, increasing the blob count has no noticeable impact on the orphan rate; some results are inconclusive and overall more data is required to have a meaningful conclusion regarding orphan rate.

stops.title: Where it stands: no PeerDAS redesign in Hegotá yet
stops.body: On the 15 October 2026 consensus-layer call, RowDAS (EIP-8371), a proposal to spread blob reconstruction across more nodes, was marked declined for inclusion in Hegotá for now: the chair read out that Teku, Lighthouse and Grandine were against and Nimbus in favour, and said it did not feel like the most urgent proposal given where blob supply and demand are today. The earlier partial reconstruction and 2D PeerDAS proposal was declined for inclusion on 19 February 2026.
stops.note: Primary source: our transcript of ACDC #189 (Alex Stokes, segments 124 to 128: client ratings against ('Teku, Lighthouse, Grandine were against'; Nimbus in favour; Lodestar and Prysm not heard), 'I think we go ahead and say DFI this for today ... where supply and demand of blobs are at today. This isn't ... the most urgent EIP'). EIP number 8371 for RowDAS is from the EIP's own page (eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8371, status Draft); the call does not say the number aloud. Says nothing about blob counts: the transcripts show no BPO3 decision as of ACDC #190 (29 Oct 2026).

excluded.reason: Ethereum Korea panel, segments 30 and 31 (PeerDAS still relies on super nodes; a stepping stone): speaker not confirmed. Four panellists, names are not spoken at the handover (an unnamed 'Alex' is addressed), so the voice could be Jun Song or Felix Lange. Only Luca Zanolini's segments 24 and 25 are used.
Staking Nerd Talk (1 May 2025): hardware requirements and BPOs, but no speaker is credited on the talk.
Staking Nerd Talk (1 May 2025): no speaker credited.
Staking Nerd Talk (1 May 2025): no speaker credited.
EthPrague 2024 'PeerDAS, Ethereum danksharding v0': no speaker credited on the talk.
Max Resnick at ETHDenver 2025 (a third of a gigagas rollup of blobs after Fusaka): the talk credits only the interviewer, Danny Nelson, so the voice cannot be named.
Debating Ethereum's Big Decision: the 'solo staking is not sustainable' line is the host reading out someone else's tweet, not the speaker's own position.
Daily Gwei, 7 June 2024 (PeerDAS made it into Pectra, as it stood then): Sassano misstates the custody share ('1/18'), and the Pectra timing is covered by s-04 and s-06.

Daily Gwei, 14 March 2024 (Dencun live, supply of blobs held back on purpose): dropped after review, because s-02 and s-03 already cover the slow, deliberate rollout. Dencun going live is now its own stop (a-dencun-live).

Daily Gwei, 11 October 2025 (conservative start, blobs at capacity): dropped after review. Sassano says he has not followed the core-dev side closely and is unsure of the numbers, and the point is made first-hand by s-12 and s-13.

Daily Gwei, 12 January 2026 (second BPO live, blob usage 4.8 against a target of 14): dropped after review in favour of Preston Van Loon's measured figures (s-16) and Daniel Knopik's demand point (s-17). Sassano's own go-slow remark in the same segment is not on the map.
Daily Gwei, 5 January 2026 (the Prysm bug at the Fusaka launch): Sassano misremembers the share of the network affected and corrects himself in the next segment.
Daily Gwei, 17 February 2025 (a Lighthouse developer's post to decouple PeerDAS from Fusaka): secondhand, and the speed question is covered first-hand by s-09.

Dankrad Feist on Epicenter, June 2021 (the first appearance of data availability sampling): dropped for length. In 2021 the 'blobs' are Eth2 data shards, not EIP-4844 blobs, and s-02 explains the idea.
Dankrad Feist on The Rollup (Nov 2025): an interviewer-led recap that repeats other stops.
Bell Curve cross-post of the Empire talk: the same words as s-10 and s-11.
Francesco D'Amato at Devcon 7: the same design as s-02, in more detail; one Francesco stop is enough.
PEEPanEIP EIP-7594 with Francesco D'Amato (Oct 2025): the same material as s-02.

EthPandaOps Fusaka testing talk, segments 0 to 11: Barnabas Busa's half of the talk. Only Parithosh Jayanthi's half is used (s-13), because Barnabas hands over at segment 11 ('I will pass it to Parry').

PEEPanEIP on EIP-7691 with Sam Calder-Mason (segments 34 and 35, 'we don't want any home stakers to drop off'): the Pectra blob increase IS part of this map's argument (a-146-decision, w-er21096-samcm), so 'about the Pectra blob increase rather than PeerDAS' is no reason. Still not used: the catalogue date, 23 February 2025, could not be confirmed (a podcast feed lists the episode on 15 March 2025), and the same author's own post gives the data first-hand and dated (w-er21096-samcm).
Leo on validator performance (Devconnect): mentions concerns about Fusaka in passing without saying what they are.

Daily Gwei, 21 June 2024, former s-04: Anthony Sassano on whether to raise blob counts with a quick hard fork or let PeerDAS in Pectra do it. A host's reading of the timing argument, not a call or a builder. The same turn is told first-hand by dapplion (s-06, blobs raised in Pectra without sampling, PeerDAS moved to Fusaka) and Mark Mackey (s-12, blob-parameter-only forks).

Empire, 19 May 2025, former s-11: Ryan Berckmans, a guest commentator, replying that Fusaka is an L2-focused upgrade and that L1 gas-limit work runs in parallel. The reply now comes first-hand from Tim Beiko on the All Core Devs call of 24 April 2025 (s-r03). Tom Dunleavy's objection (s-10) stays: no first-hand voice made that critique.

Are blobs good for Ethereum? (Devcon 7, 13 Nov 2024): a panel on whether blobs should pay more or be free. That is a blob-pricing and value-capture debate, not how PeerDAS reached Ethereum; the matched passage is only the moderator's introduction.

PeerDAS and BPO hardforks (Fusaka Files, 3 Nov 2025): Tim Beiko explains the blob-parameter-only forks. The same reasoning is told first-hand by Mark Mackey (s-12) and in the EIP-7892 thread; the episode is an explainer, not an argument.

Ansgar Dietrichs and Barnabe Monnot at Devconnect (17 Nov 2025): a clear PeerDAS explainer and the aim of 3x blob throughput a year. The pace is already told by Mike Neuder (s-03) and the launch framing by Preston Van Loon (s-14).

Danksharding Workshop, Devcon Bogota (14 Oct 2022): six speakers, no speaker labels in the captions, and Danny Ryan, who presents the networking section, is not credited on the talk. The origin of sampling is told by Dankrad Feist (s-18) and in Danny Ryan's own post (w-er16541-djrtwo).

All Core Devs - Consensus #160 (10 Jul 2025): read. Segments 79 to 87 are the call where the shape of the Fusaka blob rollout was agreed (only two blob-parameter forks scheduled with Fusaka): now a-160-stokes and a-160-decision. The getBlobs API change (Raul Kripalani, Alex Stokes, segments 51 to 52) stays out: engine API, no argument about pace.

All Core Devs - Consensus #155 (17 Apr 2025): read. Segments 60 to 65 are where EIP-7892 was moved to scheduled-for-inclusion in Fusaka (now a-155-decision); the config format and emergency-override argument (segments 16 to 31, Dustin Brody, Parithosh Jayanthi) is client configuration. The builder API blob-size question (segments 127 to 130) is an implementation worry, not on the map.

All Core Devs - Execution #209 (10 Apr 2025): read. Beyond 'Fusaka scope and the gas-limit order' it holds (a) the finalised list of considered EIPs, with PeerDAS and the EOF EIPs scheduled, (b) the blob-parameter fork EIP accepted as considered, (c) the first call for a blobs-per-transaction cap (Ben Adams, segment 205, broad support) and (d) the first discussion of the blob fee floor (Anders Elowsson and Ansgar Dietrichs, segments 159 to 179, now a-154-anders). Not used as quotes: (a) and (b) are told by s-r02 and a-155-decision, (c) is a size cap (see the EIP-7594 ledger row), (d) is covered by the 3 Apr 2025 pitch.
All Core Devs - Execution #222 (9 Oct 2025): scanned. BPO values in the genesis config file and a Lighthouse peer issue at the BPO1 boundary: client configuration, not an argument about PeerDAS.

Talks in the catalogue with no transcript, so not quotable (a gap, not a choice): KZG and EIP 4844 parts 1 and 2 (Qi Zhou, 2022), Distributed data availability sampling with PeerDAS and future developments (Dankrad Feist, Jul 2024), The Journey from Blobs to Data Availability Sampling (Csaba Kiraly, Jul 2024), Are Blobs really blobs? (Giulio Rebuffo, Jul 2024), Standardizing Ethereum metrics: PeerDAS and FOCIL retrospective (Katya Riazantseva, 2025), At the Intersection of Data Availability Sampling and Sharded Mempools (Leo BG, 2025), Mechanisms for Unlocking Idle Blobspace (Raluca Diugan, 2025), Ethereum Fusaka (Mandarin, May 2026).

Series with speaker labels absent and no credited speakers (The Daily Gwei, Staking Nerd Talk, PeerDAS and ACD testing breakouts) cannot be quoted; the Daily Gwei episodes already considered are listed above (x-08 to x-11).

Written sources read and left out: Alex Stokes's HackMD 'blob/acc in 2025' (the programmatic doubling schedule that BPO forks followed): the page shows no publication date, so a dated stop cannot be made; Potuz's 'Faster block/blob propagation' (ethresear.ch 21370, Jan 2025): a propagation-layer proposal not tied to the PeerDAS argument; Mike Neuder's 'On the future of the blob mempool' (22613) repeats the point of his EthCC talk (s-22); EIP-7892 thread posts on naming (Sam Wilson, Tim Beiko, felipe): jokes and minor; ethPandaOps 'Fusaka bandwidth estimation' and devnet-5 BPO analysis: measurements already told by Barnabas Busa (s-r05); Hsiao-Wei Wang's EIP-7594 thread (post 1 is links; later posts are bug reports): minor; Prysm's 'Recommendation for Fusaka' (HackMD, shows no date; its position is already on the call, s-r02): minor. The Sigma Prime post on a higher starting blob count was found on 10 Nov 2026 (w-sigma-chen-2025-06-26).

Fork and test-network logistics, not arguments: Fusaka testnet dates (Holesky 1 Oct, Sepolia 14 Oct, Hoodi 28 Oct 2025) and the BPO dates on each, the Pectra testnet dates (Feb to Mar 2025), the Hegota headliner proposal window, the 'temperature check' calls on the Fusaka mainnet date (ACDC #167, 16 Oct, and ACDE #223, 23 Oct 2025). The mainnet and BPO dates that matter are in s-decision.

Sunnyside Labs devnet measurements quoted inside Jimmy Chen's post (13 and 23 June 2025: block delay above 3 s near 50 blobs and above 4 s near 70): not a separate source; the argument made from them is w-sigma-chen-2025-06-26.
Capacity figures in explainers (12-blob test target, 50 or 72 blobs theoretical, 6 to 48, 8x): restatements; the first-hand numbers are on s-16, s-13 and s-r05.
Christine Kim's April 2025 estimate that Fusaka would ship in 2026: a forecast, not a decision, and overtaken by events (mainnet 3 Dec 2025).
Fredrik Svantes's Ethereum Protocol Upgrade Process document: process; not an argument about blobs.
Protocol Update 001 (5 Aug 2025): not read; Protocol Update 002 (22 Aug 2025) repeats its blob decisions.
ePBS and FOCIL scoping (Glamsterdam and Hegota): covered by their own maps.
Fusaka security audit competition (announced 26 Sep 2025): no argument on the map.
Libp2p multiplexing (drop mplex for yamux and QUIC): networking implementation, not blob pace.
EIP-7935 (60M default gas limit): L1 gas scaling; the priority argument is s-10 and s-r03.

All Core Devs - Consensus #144 (17 Oct 2024): the call notes (144.10) record Francis Li of Base presenting the case for raising blob capacity in Pectra (target 5, maximum 8); the matching transcript passage (around segment 171) is unlabeled, so no line can be attributed, and the slides are a Google Doc that was not saved. The Pectra increase is on the map through a-146-decision, w-er21096-samcm and w-er21138-cortze.

All Core Devs - Execution #201 (5 Dec 2024): read in the transcript (segments 41 to 56) and the ethereum/pm notes. EIP-7762 (minimum blob price): the case for (price discovery too slow after each change in demand, rollups do not want a volatile first-price market, a speaker urging it: the base fee can rise only 8% per block after the throughput increase) and the case against (very early, do not meddle with the price mechanism yet) are both in unlabeled segments (the talk credits nobody for them), so no line can be attributed. It was deferred a week, later went stagnant (EIPs history, 8 Feb 2026) and EIP-7918 replaced it for Fusaka (a-154-anders). The update fraction for EIP-7691 was chosen on this call (EIP-7691 ledger row).

All Core Devs - Consensus #143 (3 Oct 2024): read in the ethereum/pm notes (143.8 and 143.9): Ansgar Dietrichs suggests including a blob target increase in Pectra and removing it later if unsafe, Potuz objects that removal is as much work as adding. No decision; the same people argue it again on #146 (a-146-potuz, a-146-ansgar).

All Core Devs - Consensus #146, other passages: the ethPandaOps presentation (segments 113 to 117) and the Migalabs bandwidth concern (segments 152 to 154) are unlabeled in the transcript, so they are told by the two written posts instead (w-er21096-samcm, w-er21138-cortze); Ahmad Bitar (segments 119 to 120, labelled) adds the gas-limit-and-block-size point, which belongs to the EIP-7623 debate, not this map.
All Core Devs - Execution #215 (3 Jul 2025): the blob-per-transaction cap moves into the PeerDAS EIP at 6 (Tim Beiko, segments 102 and 112): a size cap, see the EIP-7594 ledger row.
All Core Devs - Execution #212 (22 May 2025): Tim Beiko's summary (segment 119) that people generally wanted the blob fee floor (EIP-7918) for the Fusaka devnets: the pitch is a-154-anders.

All Core Devs - Consensus #174 (5 Feb 2026): Leo presents the partial reconstruction and 2D PeerDAS proposal (segments 80 to 85; the proposal itself is w-mg27652-leobago) and Alex Stokes says cell-level messaging can ship between forks and nobody is rushing another BPO (segment 43): used as context in the note of a-175-decision, not as a quote.

spec_changes.change: Fee market update: blobs get their own EIP-1559-style price (PR 5707).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not identified. Likely one of the EIP-4844 implementers calls of 25 Oct to 8 Nov 2022; those calls were only keyword-scanned.
spec_changes.why_not: How the blob price moves, not how many blobs; the map's fee-market argument is the later EIP-7918 (a-154-anders). Blocker: the agreeing call was not identified.

spec_changes.change: Reduce Throughput (PR 5863): target 8 and maximum 16 blobs per block cut to a target of 2 and a maximum of 4 (about 0.25 and 0.5 MB).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Argued on ACDE #149 (10 Nov 2022: Micah Zoltu, Dankrad Feist, Ansgar Dietrichs, Andrew Ashikhmin). The call that agreed the cut was not identified.

spec_changes.change: Disable blob transaction broadcast: nodes announce blob transactions instead of pushing them (PR 5930).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not identified (EIP-4844 implementers call #5, 22 Nov 2022, not read).
spec_changes.why_not: Mempool DoS mitigation; implementation detail with no argument on the map. Blocker: call not read.

spec_changes.change: More sane limits on blobs per transaction (constant 2**24 to 2**12; PR 6500).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not identified (EIP-4844 implementers calls of Feb 2023, not read).
spec_changes.why_not: A size constant for encoding, not a policy on blob counts.

spec_changes.change: Decouple blobs: blobs travel beside the block, not in it (PR 6610).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not identified; call #22 (15 May 2023) opens with the spec changes agreed the week before. Not read in full.
spec_changes.why_not: Design of how blobs travel; no argument on the map, and Ansgar Dietrichs only refers to it on ACDE #163 as extra robustness. Blocker: call not read in full.

spec_changes.change: Increase blob throughput: target 2 and maximum 4 raised to a target of 3 and a maximum of 6 (PR 7154).
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDE #163 (8 June 2023): proposed by Dankrad Feist with mainnet load-test data; no objection voiced on that call to trying it on devnet 6 (Tim Beiko); revisited on EIP-4844 implementers call #24 (12 June 2023), where an execution developer says he would vote against but leaves the decision to consensus-layer developers (that call has no speaker labels, so it cannot be quoted).

spec_changes.change: Move to Final; blob base fee renamed 'base fee per blob gas'.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Dencun mainnet 13 March 2024.

spec_changes.change: EIP created: PeerDAS (sampling on gossip and peer requests).
spec_changes.agreed_at: Design first argued in ethresear.ch (Sep 2023 onward) and scheduled for Pectra, then moved out on ACDC #142 (19 Sep 2024) and into Fulu on ACDC #145 (31 Oct 2024).

spec_changes.change: Cell proofs are built by the blob-transaction sender and carried in the blob transaction's network wrapper with a wrapper version byte.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Proposed on ACDC #150 (6 Feb 2025); the version byte confirmed as final on ACDE #208 (27 Mar 2025, Francesco D'Amato and Felix Lange, Alex Stokes: merge as soon as possible).
spec_changes.why_not: The agreeing call (ACDE #208) is not a stop of its own: it only confirms a version byte for a design already told by s-r01. Judgment call, flagged.

spec_changes.change: A limit of 6 blobs per transaction is written into the EIP.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Raised by Ben Adams on ACDE #209 (10 Apr 2025: 'do we want to limit the number of blobs per transaction'); moved from the BPO EIP to the PeerDAS EIP and set at 6 on ACDE #215 (3 Jul 2025, Tim Beiko).
spec_changes.why_not: A size cap for the pool and for packing blocks, with broad support on both calls; not a dispute about PeerDAS pace or priority.

spec_changes.change: Rationale: fix the upper bound probability.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not a behaviour change.
spec_changes.why_not: Corrects the maths in the rationale; no behaviour changes.

spec_changes.change: EIP updated with the blob counts: target 6 and maximum 9 (it was drafted in April 2024).
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDC #146 (28 Nov 2024): after the ethPandaOps data and objections from Potuz, Alex Stokes said he was hearing a lot of support for 6/9 and listed 7691 for Pectra devnet 5.

spec_changes.change: Update fraction set to 5007716 (the middle sensitivity between the 3 and 6 choices).
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDE #201 (5 Dec 2024, Ansgar Dietrichs).
spec_changes.why_not: A fee-sensitivity constant that follows from 6/9; the argument for it is a-146-ansgar.

spec_changes.change: Decoupled from EIP-7742 (blob count set from the consensus layer); the blob counts are carried by EIP-7840 instead.
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDC #147 (12 Dec 2024), reaffirmed on ACDE #202 (19 Dec 2024); 7742 dropped for complexity and Pectra delay.
spec_changes.why_not: Which mechanism sets the counts; it did not change what they were. Blocker: ACDC #147 not read, the account is from the ethereum/pm notes of ACDE #202.

spec_changes.change: EIP created: blob-parameter-only forks.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Pitched in March 2025; ACDC #154 (3 Apr 2025: everyone wants PeerDAS and BPO) then scheduled for inclusion on ACDC #155 (17 Apr 2025).

spec_changes.change: Per-transaction blob limit added to blobSchedule (moved to EIP-7594 on 14 Jul 2025).
spec_changes.why_not: Same cap as the EIP-7594 row above.

spec_changes.change: Update fractions corrected for the BPO schedule.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Values from the Devnet 5 analysis reported on ACDC #165 (18 Sep 2025).

spec_changes.change: Clarify how the blob schedule is used in base fee computations.
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDE #222 (9 Oct 2025): execution developers (Marius van der Wijden) want an explicit schedule; consensus-layer convention reuses the previous fork's value; agreed to touch the blob schedule only with BPO forks.
spec_changes.why_not: Client-configuration convention (x-n08); no dispute about blob counts.

spec_changes.change: New specification: blob base fee bounded by execution cost (BLOB_BASE_COST); text and figures rewritten after the first version of 26 Mar 2025.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Pitched on ACDC #154 (3 Apr 2025, Anders Elowsson) and ACDE #209 (10 Apr 2025); Tim Beiko's ACDE #212 summary (22 May 2025): people generally wanted it; in Fusaka devnets from then.

spec_changes.change: Use the current block's blobSchedule when computing the floor.
spec_changes.agreed_at: ACDE #218 (14 Aug 2025, Lightclient).
spec_changes.why_not: Fee-computation detail in the same EIP; no argument.

spec_changes.change: BLOB_BASE_COST fixed at 2**13 and figures updated.
spec_changes.agreed_at: Not identified.
spec_changes.why_not: Tuning of the floor's size. Blocker: the call that set 2**13 was not found; judged minor.
